While the central characters, Mara and Julian, are well-developed and complex, several minor characters are extremely flat and suddenly appear without proper introduction simply to fill out the setting or advance a scene. At the beginning of the story, the other occupants of the car are referred to only as Celia and "four other residents" (or "the driver"). Later, names and labels like "Lyle," "Ken," and "two painters" are abruptly dropped into the narrative with no prior introduction or context. Because the reader doesn't even know how these labels map onto the original group in the car, these characters feel like underdeveloped placeholders rather than organic parts of the story.
